title: Global Mangrove Watch v3 range limits stayed fixed in 1996-2020 and omit stands up to 4 degrees poleward; freezes below -6 C in Louisiana and Gulf Florida removed 12% of mapped area, which recovered
abstract: Question: do winter freezes, not winter means, control mangrove area at poleward range limits, and can the global annual Global Mangrove Watch v3 maps (GMW v3, 1996-2020, L-band radar) test this across regions and periods? Method: we read all 470 GMW v3 tiles at |latitude| >= 18 degrees for 11 years by HTTP range requests, summed mangrove area by 0.25-degree cell, and matched cells to NOAA CPC daily minimum temperature (0.5 degree, 2006-2020, two quality-control steps). We modelled area change between consecutive annual maps in one sensor era (12,922 cell-pairs) with map-pair fixed effects, and we compared GMW limits with GBIF occurrence records. Results: (1) In all 20 range-limit boxes, the most poleward mapped mangrove moved by 0.094 degrees or less from 1996 to 2020. CC0/CC BY GBIF records put mangroves 0.7-4 degrees beyond the GMW limit in Texas, Atlantic Florida, Western Australia, southern Brazil and New Zealand. The GMW v3 method permits gain only within 500 m of the 2010 baseline, so it cannot record poleward expansion. (2) Coldest nights below -4 C occurred in only 35 cell-pairs (Louisiana, Gulf Florida, one Zhejiang cell). Mapped area changed by -12.3% after nights below -6 C (pair-FE dlog -0.089, 95% CI -0.178 to -0.0001), with no loss at -4 to -6 C. Louisiana cells lost 7.8% after the January 2018 freeze and regained 14.5% the next year, which agrees with field resprouting. (3) Among frost-exposed cells, degrees below 0 C predicted loss (slope -0.0068 per C, p = 0.04) but the winter-mean anomaly did not (p = 0.72). (4) Transfer tests between East Asia and the Americas, and between sensor eras, failed or could not decide; an East Asian frost signal was not robust to map-pair effects. Limitations: few freeze events, 0.5-degree temperatures colder than coastal sites, radar that sees woody structure more than leaf loss, and GBIF records that can include planted trees. GMW v3 is not suitable for testing climate-driven mangrove range expansion.

display.caption: GBIF mangrove records from 2010-2025 (CC0 or CC BY only) poleward of the GMW v3 range limit in each region. The GMW limit moved by at most 0.094 degrees in the 11 maps of 1996-2020. The numbers give the open-licence records and, in brackets, the records under all licences.

Mapped GMW v3 area change between consecutive annual maps, by the coldest daily minimum (CPC 0.5-degree grid) of the winter between the maps, 2007-2020. Error bars: 95% bootstrap over 1-degree tiles. Only Louisiana and Gulf Florida had nights below -4 C; the East Asian bars rest on 22 cell-pairs and are not robust.

Mapped area of cells that went below -4 C and of the other cells in the same region, around the January 2010 freeze (Gulf Florida) and the January 2018 freeze (Louisiana). The grey band is the freeze winter.
